approachQuestion.prompt:
Distinct mixture ratios

A read-only array holds n pairs (p,q), representing exact rational values p/q. Count the number of distinct mathematical values. A denominator may be negative but is never zero; all representations of zero denote the same value.

Example 1: [(1,2),(-2,-4),(0,7),(0,-3),(3,-6)] -> 3, for 1/2,0,-1/2.
Example 2: [(2,3),(4,6)] -> 1.

Constraints and assumptions: 1 <= n <= 200000; -10^9 <= p,q <= 10^9 and q!=0. Do not modify the input. Use exact arithmetic and a deterministic comparison-based method; randomized hashing is not part of the execution model. Return only a count. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Reduce each fraction by an iterative gcd and normalize the denominator sign, mapping zero to (0,1). Store the pairs, sort lexicographically by bottom-up mergesort with one reusable buffer, and count adjacent changes.
options.feedback: Each rational value has exactly one reduced positive-denominator representation. Exact pair equality therefore matches value equality; sorting groups duplicates deterministically.

options.text: Perform the same normalization into an array. For each pair, compare it with all earlier normalized pairs, counting it only when no earlier pair matches.
options.feedback: Canonicalization is correct, but repeatedly searching all previous pairs leaves avoidable duplicate-comparison work.

options.text: Sort copies of the original (p,q) pairs lexicographically and count unequal adjacent pairs.
options.feedback: For [(1,2),(2,4)] this counts 2 instead of 1 because equal values can have different representations.

options.text: Count distinct truncated integer quotients p/q instead of exact rational values.
options.feedback: For [(1,2),(1,3)] both quotients truncate to zero, but the two rational values are distinct.

feedback.reason: Canonicalize signed rational values before deterministic duplicate counting.
details: For every pair, make the denominator positive and divide numerator and denominator by gcd(abs(p),abs(q)), using iterative remainder reduction; zero becomes (0,1). Save normalized pairs in a fresh array. Sort them lexicographically using bottom-up mergesort with a reusable n-pair buffer, then count adjacent changes.

Move sign to the numerator and divide both terms by their gcd; every zero ratio becomes (0,1). Equal normalized pairs then represent equal rational values. Floating division could merge or separate values incorrectly.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (normalize-sort). Let n be the number of fractions and M=max(2,max(abs(p),abs(q))) across the input. Analyze normalization plus the stated bottom-up mergesort. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

feedback.reason: Normalize n pairs, then comparison-sort them using linear helper arrays.
details: Each iterative gcd uses at most logarithmic work in M, attained by consecutive Fibonacci magnitudes; all n reductions contribute n log M in the worst case. Bottom-up mergesort performs n log(n+1) comparison work even for repeated keys. The normalized array and one reusable merge buffer each hold n pairs. All of these arrays are auxiliary because the output is only a scalar count.
Time: O(n log M + n log(n + 1)).

“O(n log M + n log(n + 1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Correct: include both gcd normalization and deterministic mergesort with its buffers.
“O(n log(n + 1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This omits the input-dependent gcd work in the stated two-parameter word-operation model.
“O(n log M + n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This describes comparing every normalized pair with earlier pairs, not merging sorted runs.
“O(n log M + n log(n + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The normalized copy and merge buffer count as auxiliary storage.
